body.x: Marking its third edition this year, FIX 2026 (Future Innovation Tech Expo), South Korea’s benchmark future industry exhibition, will be held from Wednesday, October 21 to Saturday, October 24 at EXCO in Daegu. Under the slogan “AI, Beyond Tech into Reality,” the expo establishes a new milestone for global industry by organically linking core technologies across four key advanced sectors: future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. Encompassing the achievements of Daegu Metropolitan City’s forward-looking industrial cultivation, leading domestic and international tech enterprises alongside promising startups will assemble to unveil next-generation, field-validated technologies poised to transform everyday life and industrial operations. Concurrently featuring international conferences, global business matchmaking sessions, and open innovation initiatives, the event is set to serve as a pivotal exchange hub leading technological collaboration and innovation far beyond Asia.

For FIX 2026, ET Manufacturing and ET Auto—two core vertical media platforms under the Economic Times, the biggest business news media of India—are joining forces to conduct collaborative on-site coverage and reporting. ET Manufacturing, specializing in in-depth analyses of the manufacturing value chain spanning smart factories, robotics, and industrial automation, and ET Auto, India’s largest automotive platform covering OEMs, tier suppliers, mobility policies, and autonomous and electric vehicle technologies, command unmatched influence in connecting the industrial spheres of both nations. Building on insights from ET Auto’s on-site reporting in 2024, ET Manufacturing is deploying an editorial team this year to deliver multidimensional global coverage spanning future mobility and advanced manufacturing automation. A joint advance interview was conducted with Dimpal Bajwa, Associate Editor of The Economic Times - Business Verticals, representing ET Manufacturing, reporting from Daegu, and Deepanshu Taumar, Deputy Editor of ET Auto and ET Manufacturing, who covered FIX 2024, to hear their perspectives on bilateral industrial cooperation and their expectations for FIX 2026.

body.x: 1. Could you introduce your media outlets to Korean readers?

ET Manufacturing is the specialized industrial manufacturing platform of The Economic Times, India’s leading financial daily, part of the Times Group. It covers the entire manufacturing value chain, spanning automotive and electric vehicles (EVs), electronics and semiconductors, capital goods, robotics and automation, process industries, and the strategic policy decisions shaping these sectors. The primary readership comprises core manufacturing decision-makers across India, including CEOs, plant heads, Chief Manufacturing Officers (CMOs), Chief Technology Officers (CTOs), procurement executives, and senior government officials. South Korea maintains deep ties with this editorial remit. Korean enterprises have established a significant manufacturing footprint in India through major capital investments across automotive, home appliances, steel, batteries, and precision components. Concurrently, India is aggressively building domestic capabilities across semiconductors, EV batteries, and electronics manufacturing—sectors where Korea commands global leadership. For Korean enterprises viewing India as a manufacturing hub, supply chain partner, or high-growth market, ET Manufacturing serves as an essential channel closely monitored by Indian industrial leadership. Beyond journalistic reporting, the organization also hosts and operates flagship executive leadership platforms across the Indian manufacturing landscape.

ET Auto is India’s premier automotive and mobility media platform, launched by The Economic Times to provide in-depth news, technical analyses, and global market intelligence. It commands unrivaled coverage encompassing OEMs, auto components, government regulatory policies, the aftermarket, and next-generation automotive technologies such as electrification and connected-car architectures. Operating within India’s dynamic mobility ecosystem—which contributes roughly 7% to national GDP and generates over 19 million jobs—ET Auto maintains deep networks with key industry associations and corporate leaders. Through exclusive industry reports, on-site plant assessments, and high-level executive roundtables and conferences, it functions as a central B2B business hub. The platform delivers a comprehensive daily newsletter to key decision-makers, including global OEM executives, policymakers, and institutional investors, and tracks critical technological developments. It is increasingly focused on South Korea’s accelerating transition toward electric mobility and advanced automotive component ecosystems.
2. What are your perspectives on current trends across industrial technology, mobility, and AI?

The biggest shift we see is AI moving from pilot projects to the shop floor. Indian manufacturers are no longer asking whether to adopt AI. They are asking how to scale it across quality inspection, predictive maintenance, energy management, and production planning. Data ownership between operations and IT teams and workforce skills now matter as much as the technology itself.

In mobility, electrification is advancing alongside software-defined vehicles and localized battery and component supply chains. Robotics and automation are becoming viable for mid-sized manufacturers, not just large OEMs, as costs fall and systems become easier to deploy. Supply chains are also being redesigned for resilience, which creates a strong opportunity for India–Korea collaboration.

body.x: 3. What key issues and topics related to FIX 2026 will interest your readership most?

FIX 2026 covers four areas: future mobility, robotics, AI and ICT, and startups. All of these closely match our audience's priorities. This year's theme, "AI, Beyond Tech into Reality," fits what Indian manufacturers care about most: practical, deployable AI rather than concepts.

Our audience is especially interested in industrial and collaborative robotics for mid-sized plants, AI for quality and predictive maintenance, EV and battery technology, including secondary batteries and components, autonomous mobility, digital twins, and partnerships with Korean startups and technology suppliers
They also want to know which Korean technologies are ready for co-development or manufacturing in India.
4. How was the experience covering FIX 2024, and what are your expectations for this year’s exhibition?

FIX 2024 showed clearly how Daegu is building an integrated platform where mobility, robotics, and ICT come together in one place. This year, we expect a stronger focus on commercial outcomes. The 2026 edition is set to be larger, with around 510 participating companies and 2,100 booths, and it adds pre-matched consultation sessions and direct overseas buyer visits to exhibitor booths. We look forward to identifying Korean innovations relevant to Indian manufacturing and bringing those stories to our readers.
5. What are your thoughts on participating as an official Global Media Award partner?

We are honored to be an official Global Media Award partner. We see our role as a bridge: bringing Korea's most innovative companies and technologies to India's manufacturing leaders, and giving Korean firms visibility in one of the world's fastest-growing manufacturing economies. India's manufacturing ambitions and Korea's technological depth complement each other. As a partner, we hope to turn that fit into lasting business relationships, and we look forward to continuing the collaboration beyond FIX through our own platforms, including the ET Global Manufacturing Conclave.

body.x: Meanwhile, ten prominent global media partners spanning Europe, the Americas, and Asia are participating as official press partners for FIX 2026, deploying on-site reporting delegations.

The international press corps includes leading technology and industry media representing their respective regions: Le Café du Geek, a French IT, lifestyle, and global tech publication; Clipset, a pioneering Spanish mobile and consumer tech outlet; Ubergizmo, a Silicon Valley-based American consumer electronics and innovative tech portal; AVING USA, an American global tech, business, and exhibition media outlet; Otaku Soken, a Japanese subculture and AI, VR, and IT convergence publication; DIGITIMES, world-renowned semiconductor and ICT supply chain media and research agency; VietnamPlus, a state-run multinational comprehensive news portal in Vietnam; ChinaByte, China’s first enterprise digital transformation (DX), IT, and AI publication; ET Manufacturing, an Indian smart factory, robotics, and manufacturing engineering media outlet; and Pokde.net, a Malaysian hardware, gaming, and mobile tech publication.

These global media partners will participate directly in on-site evaluations during the event, including the FIX Innovation Awards press conference and the Global Media Selected Best of FIX 2026 Media Awards, reporting from the front lines of technological developments by innovative enterprises shaping the future of South Korea’s high-tech landscape.
